problem.original_text: Find the intersection points of $$y=2x+1$$ and $$y=x^2$$. Include a plot of both curves and mark the intersection points.
problem.normalized_text: Find the intersection points of $$y=2x+1$$ and $$y=x^2$$. Include a plot of both curves and mark the intersection points.

steps.title: Set equations equal
steps.explanation: Intersections satisfy 2x+1 = x^2, so solve x^2 - 2x -1 = 0.

steps.title: Solve quadratic
steps.explanation: Use quadratic formula: x = [2 ± sqrt(4+4)]/2 = 1 ± sqrt(2).

steps.title: Find y-coordinates
steps.explanation: Plug x into y=2x+1 to get corresponding y values.

steps.title: List intersection points
steps.explanation: The two real intersection points are (1+√2, 3+2√2) and (1-√2, 3-2√2).

steps.title: Plotting decision
steps.explanation: Graphing both y=x^2 and y=2x+1 on a domain showing both intersections.

steps.title: Plot details
steps.explanation: Use domain x in [-2,4] and sample sufficiently to display curves and mark intersection points.
